overall: mean of the four axis means (each axis weighted equally regardless of how many criteria it holds)
note: The input is the game's Ren'Py script (script.rpy) — the actual built artifact. Judge it as a player would: the only knowledge you have is what the script shows on screen (dialogue, narration, menus, and scene/show staging). You do NOT know the author's intent, the planned theme, or any character bible. Trace paths by following menus and jumps between labels.

criteria.name: hook_strength
criteria.description: Starting from the start label, the opening grabs the player fast — a concrete dramatic question or a destabilizing event by the end of the first scene. Test: if the opening is scene-setting, exposition, or mood with nothing at stake by the time the first menu or scene change arrives, score 0-40. If something the player needs resolved is already in play within the first scene, score 70+. Atmosphere alone is not a hook.

criteria.name: plot_coherence
criteria.description: Following one path start to ending, events cause one another and characters drive them. Test: any major turn that happens for the plot's convenience — a reversal nothing set up, a character acting against everything shown to reach a beat — scores 0-40. If each beat is the visible consequence of an earlier one, score 70+. Coincidence that creates trouble is fine; coincidence that resolves it is not.

criteria.name: thematic_depth
criteria.description: Played through, the game has something to say — it puts a genuine tension under pressure rather than asserting a lesson. Test: if it moralizes, states its point in narration, or only ever weights one side of its central conflict, score 0-40. If different scenes or paths embody defensible opposing answers so the player feels the tension instead of being told it, score 70+. You are inferring this from the script alone; no stated theme exists.

criteria.name: emotional_pacing
criteria.description: Intensity is shaped across the playthrough — escalation, release, contrast — not a flat line. Test: if every scene runs at the same emotional pitch (all crisis, or all quiet), or tension never builds toward the choices and endings, score 0-40. If there is a deliberate rise with beats of contrast (a quiet moment before a confrontation) that make the peaks land, score 70+.

criteria.name: ending_satisfaction
criteria.description: Trace at least two endings via the menus and jumps. Each lands with finality and feels earned by the path that reached it. Test: an ending that trails off, restates the setup, or could be swapped onto a different path without changing meaning scores 0-40. If each ending is a distinct, earned conclusion the player understands arriving at, score 70+.

criteria.name: distinctiveness
criteria.description: Each character reads as one particular person, not an archetype with adjectives. Test: an interchangeable cast, or characters defined only by stacked traits, scores 0-40. If — with the speaker name tags mentally removed — you could still tell who is talking from vocabulary, rhythm, and concerns alone, score 70+.

criteria.name: depth
criteria.description: Characters show interiority beyond their plot function — wants in tension, contradictions, things they will not say. Test: characters who exist only to advance the plot or deliver information score 0-40. If at least the central characters carry a want that collides with another of their wants or with the protagonist's, visible in how they behave under pressure, score 70+. An antagonist whose only trait is opposition fails.

criteria.name: consistency
criteria.description: Within a single traced path, each character's voice, values, and knowledge hold together — no personality whiplash, no referencing events they could not have witnessed on that path. Test: any unearned out-of-character turn, or a character knowing something that only happened on a branch the player did not take, scores 0-40. If behavior coheres scene to scene and changes only where the story motivates it, score 70+.

criteria.name: arc_movement
criteria.description: At least the protagonist is changed by the events of a path; the person at the ending is not the person at the start, and the path caused the difference. Test: a protagonist identical in outlook from first scene to last scores 0-40. If there is visible movement — a belief abandoned, a fear faced, a bond transformed — that the events made happen, score 70+. The change must be dramatized, not announced.

criteria.name: relationship_dynamics
criteria.description: Relationships have specific texture and shift over the playthrough rather than sitting as generic ally/enemy labels. Test: flat or static relationships, or bonds asserted but never shown, score 0-40. If relationships carry history and friction and shift because of what happens between the characters across scenes, score 70+.

criteria.name: dialogue_craft
criteria.description: Lines feel spoken by distinct people, conversations have real turn-taking — questions answered or pointedly dodged, lines reacting to the line before — and emotion comes through what characters say, avoid, or deflect, never by announcing it ('I feel betrayed' scores 0-40). If, with speaker tags hidden, you could still identify who speaks, and no exchange is filler, score 75+.

criteria.name: prose_quality
criteria.description: The narration lines (quoted text with no speaker) are precise and controlled — no purple prose, cliche, or filler. Test: cliche-laden, vague, or overwrought narration ('a chill ran down her spine', 'time seemed to stop') scores 0-40. If narration is concrete and economical, with a controlled voice that earns its images, score 70+.

criteria.name: show_vs_tell
criteria.description: Emotional states and character traits are conveyed through action, dialogue, and on-screen staging (scene/show) rather than stated by the narrator. Test: narration that labels feelings or traits ('she was nervous', 'he was a cruel man') scores 0-40. If the player infers states from what characters do, how they speak, and what the staging shows, score 70+.

criteria.name: choice_meaningfulness
criteria.description: Menu choice labels read as real decisions with visible stakes, and the lines immediately before each menu build toward the decision. Test: scene-summary or interchangeable labels ('Go left' / 'Go right'), or a menu that appears with no buildup, scores 0-40. If each menu presents a genuine dilemma the preceding scene made urgent, score 70+.

criteria.name: branch_coherence
criteria.description: Trace at least two distinct paths from start to an ending by following menus and jumps between labels. Each path reads coherently on its own: every event a character references actually happened earlier ON THAT PATH, and where branches merge back the result reads cleanly regardless of which choice led in. Test: any line that assumes events from a branch the player did not take scores 0-35. If both traced paths hold together causally, score 70+.

criteria.name: path_differentiation
criteria.description: Different menu choices lead to genuinely different experiences, not cosmetic variants of one path. Compare the branches and their endings. Test: branches that reconverge to the same beats and near-identical endings, differing only in flavor text, score 0-40. If the choices change events, character outcomes, and the conclusion reached, so a replay reveals a different story, score 70+.
